questions.q: What question does the summary say you should ask before investing in a company?
a: Would I buy this whole business if I could?
Will the stock price rise again this week?
How many shares can I afford to buy today?
What do other investors think of the company?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says imagining a full purchase forces you to do your homework and notice shady practices.

questions.q: What is an economic moat in the summary?
a: A lasting advantage that protects a company from rivals
A tax break granted to new businesses
A loan used to buy shares on margin
A fee paid to a stockbroker
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains a moat as a kind of monopoly position that keeps a company profitable for years.

questions.q: Which company does the summary use as an example of a strong brand moat?
a: Coca-Cola, recognized all over the world
A startup in its first funding round
A retailer running temporary sales
A bank with a popular chief executive
questions.why: Lesson 2 says even remote communities wear Coca-Cola shirts, showing the reach of its brand.

questions.q: What is the margin of safety in the summary?
a: The gap between a stock's true value and its price
The amount of cash kept in a savings account
The fee charged when you sell a stock
The number of shares held in a portfolio
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines it as the value per share you calculate minus the current share price.

questions.q: How large a margin of safety does the author recommend before buying?
a: At least 50 percent
At least 10 percent
At least 25 percent
At least 75 percent
questions.why: Lesson 3 gives a stock worth $200 trading at $100 as a 50 percent margin, the minimum the author advises.
